question: A grants officer facing a deadline has used Claude to draft eligibility determinations for ninety applicants, and each determination will be sent directly to the applicant. Under Anthropic's Usage Policy, which two things must happen before the determinations are issued? Select two.
options: A) Claude is asked to review its own determinations and flag any it is unsure about.
B) A qualified officer checks each determination against the published eligibility rules.
C) Each determination that goes out tells the applicant that Claude helped produce it.
D) Only the determinations that look borderline are pulled out for a person to read.
E) Claude is recorded as the decision-maker, so responsibility for each one rests with the tool.
correct_answers: B) A qualified officer checks each determination against the published eligibility rules.
C) Each determination that goes out tells the applicant that Claude helped produce it.
explanations: Self-review is not verification. A determination that misread a rule will often be reported as confident, so the cases most in need of attention stay hidden.

Correct. The Usage Policy requires that a qualified professional review a decision directly affecting individuals before it is finalized. Eligibility for funding is such a decision, so each one needs checking against the actual rules rather than sampling or spot checks.

Correct. When model outputs are presented directly to individuals, the Usage Policy requires disclosing to them that AI helped produce the decision, so each determination sent to an applicant must say that Claude helped produce it. An internal file note alone would not tell the applicant.
Borderline cases are identified by the same process being verified, so anything wrongly classed as clear-cut is exactly what this approach fails to catch.

Responsibility cannot be handed to the tool. The Usage Policy states that the user or their organization is responsible for the accuracy and appropriateness of the information, so recording Claude as the decision-maker leaves no accountable person and does nothing to make the determinations correct.
